narrative.overview:
Akooti's interface behaves like a precision instrument in a locked case: dark machined
surfaces, a single lit indicator, and no ornament that is not doing work. Every screen is
a readout of state the user must be able to trust — which vault is open, which folder is
scoped, which secret is currently revealed — and the design earns that trust by staying
quiet. Density is a feature: this is a tool for a developer at a keyboard, so information
is packed tight and the chrome stays out of the way.

The material is flat. Depth is not implied by light falling on surfaces; it is drawn with
1px borders and a six-step tonal ramp from near-black to a lifted panel grey. A card is
not "above" the page, it is a distinct plane. The one piece of colour with authorship is
Signal Blue, and its scarcity is the point — it marks the active row, the primary action,
the focused control and a live one-time code, nothing else.

Copy is sober technical French: plain sentences, no superlatives, and an error says what
failed and what to do next. The visual system never decorates a security decision; it
surfaces it — refusal, masking, scope and expiry are all visible states rather than
modals that appear after the fact.
keyCharacteristics: Dark is the canonical theme; light is a remapped token set, not a second design.
Flat at rest: 1px borders and a tonal ramp carry all separation.
One accent, used on ≤10% of a screen.
14px base, compact 0.45–0.55rem control padding, 2px inter-row gaps.
Every state is also text, never colour alone.
Fully keyboard-operable: a 2px accent focus ring is never removed.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue covers ≤10% of any screen. If a layout needs a second accent to make sense, the layout is wrong, not the palette.

rules.name: The Semantic Variable Rule
rules.body: A component never names a colour literal; it consumes a token. A raw hex inside a component rule is a bug, not a variation. (Two documented exceptions carry a `var(--x, fallback)` pair: `--danger` and `--warn` in the health and audit rows.)

rules.name: The Dark-Is-Canonical Rule
rules.body: New tokens are authored dark first. Light theme is a key-by-key remap of the same variable names in `:root[data-theme="light"]`; a token that only exists in one theme is incomplete.

rules.name: The Uppercase Is Structure Rule
rules.body: Text-transform: uppercase with positive tracking is reserved for structure labels — section headings, step names, type markers, stat keys. Never uppercase a sentence, an error, or a button label.

rules.name: The Masked Is Muted Rule
rules.body: A hidden secret is rendered as muted, letter-spaced dots in `--text-muted`; a revealed secret switches to full `--text` on a Signal Wash, zero letter-spacing. The visual difference between masked and revealed must be legible at a glance without reading the characters.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Nothing gains elevation on hover — hover is a background shift on the tonal ramp. If you reach for a shadow to separate two elements, use a hairline instead.

rules.name: The Two-Shadow Rule
rules.body: The system owns exactly two shadow values. A third means someone mistook a border for a shadow.

rules.name: The Three-Radius Rule
rules.body: Before adding a number, ask which of the three jobs the surface has — touch, group, or cover. A fourth radius means a fourth job, and there isn't one.

rules.name: The Border-Over-Fill Rule
rules.body: A new state is introduced with a border colour plus a washed background, not with a solid fill. Solid fills belong to the primary button and the active surfaces, and they are rare on purpose.
